[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"EC2 Instance Lifecycle: Launch, Stop, Terminate"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances have a lifecycle that includes various states. Understanding these states is crucial for managing your AWS resources effectively. This tutorial covers the key stages: Launch, Stop, and Terminate."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Launching an EC2 Instance"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Launching an EC2 instance involves several steps. First, you select an Amazon Machine Image (AMI), which provides the operating system, application server, and applications. Then, you choose an instance type, which determines the hardware configuration (CPU, memory, storage). Finally, you configure security groups, key pairs, and other settings."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select an AMI: Choose an AMI that meets your requirements (e.g., Amazon Linux 2, Ubuntu, Windows Server)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Choose an Instance Type: Select an instance type based on your workload's resource needs (e.g., t2.micro, t3.medium, m5.large)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure Security Groups: Define firewall rules to control inbound and outbound traffic to your instance. For example, allow SSH (port 22) for Linux instances or RDP (port 3389) for Windows instances."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select a Key Pair: Choose a key pair to securely connect to your instance using SSH or RDP."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to launch an EC2 instance:
aws ec2 run-instances \
    --image-id ami-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
    --instance-type t2.micro \
    --key-name my-key-pair \
    --security-group-ids sg-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
    --subnet-id subnet-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Stopping an EC2 Instance"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Stopping an EC2 instance gracefully shuts down the operating system and then powers down the instance. When an instance is stopped, you are not charged for instance usage, but you are charged for any EBS volumes attached to the instance. The instance retains its EBS-backed root volume and any other attached EBS volumes."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The instance transitions to the 'stopping' state, then to the 'stopped' state."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can start a stopped instance at any time, and it will return to its previous state (e.g., running applications will resume)."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The public IP address associated with the instance may change when it is started after being stopped, unless you are using an Elastic IP address."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to stop an EC2 instance:
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Terminating an EC2 Instance"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Terminating an EC2 instance permanently deletes the instance. When an instance is terminated, you stop paying for it. By default, EBS-backed instances have their root volumes deleted upon termination. However, you can configure the root volume to be retained. Any other attached EBS volumes are not deleted by default."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The instance transitions to the 'shutting-down' state, then to the 'terminated' state."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Once an instance is terminated, it cannot be started again. All data on the instance store volumes is lost."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Before terminating an instance, ensure you have backed up any important data."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to terminate an EC2 instance:
aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding the EC2 instance lifecycle is essential for managing your AWS resources effectively. Launch instances to run your applications, stop them to save costs when they are not needed, and terminate them when they are no longer required. Remember to back up your data before terminating an instance."}]
